gap: No result ChatGPT got lists the Fluance RT80. Fluance sells it for $249.99, within a dollar of ChatGPT's $249 AT-LP70X pick, and gives it a switchable preamp that bypasses all electronics, an adjustable counterweight and anti-skate, 0.2% wow and flutter and ≥67 dB A-weighted S/N. No result notes either that Fluance's own store prices the RT81+ ($349.99) the same as the RT82 ($349.99), which has no preamp.
standout_why: I compared against platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp (RT81 $299.99, AT-LP60X $179, AT-LP70X $249, LP120XUSB $349, PS-LX3BT $348), valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives (LP70X $249, RT81 $299.99, LP60XBT $279, LP120XUSB $349, PS-LX310BT $448, with spec numbers), thebrickfantastic.com (no prices), stylusandsound.com (names the RT81+ but gives no prices) and fewbetter.com (names no models). None of them names or prices the RT80. None gives the RT81+ price or compares it with the RT82. None prices the AT-LP70XBT or the Pro-Ject T1 EVO Phono, though stylusandsound names the T1 EVO Phono without a price. Platterandplinth already says the RT81's AT95E is listed as discontinued, so that point is not new.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's picks but adds a same-price alternative. At about $250 the shopper can choose the AT-LP70X for full automation or the Fluance RT80 for an adjustable tonearm, a preamp bypass and published 0.2% wow and flutter / 67 dB S/N figures. Fluance prices the RT81+ the same as the RT82, so a shopper who wants a preamp pays nothing extra at $349.99. The RT81+ also gets the current VM95E elliptical cartridge in place of the RT81's AT95E, which is only $50 cheaper. That makes the RT81+ the better buy than the RT81 in the manual-deck lane.
